slot.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
slot.subtopic: de Broglie wavelength of accelerated charges
slot.brief: Same potential difference accelerates two particles with different mass and charge; find the ratio of their de Broglie wavelengths without needing the exact formula values.

stem: A proton and an $\alpha$ particle are accelerated from rest through the same potential difference. Taking the $\alpha$ particle’s mass as $4m_p$ and its charge as $2e$, what is the ratio of their de Broglie wavelengths, $\lambda_p: \lambda_\alpha$?

verdicts.working: For acceleration from rest, p = sqrt(2mqV) and wavelength is inversely proportional to momentum. Thus lambda_p/lambda_alpha = sqrt((4m_p)(2e)/(m_p e)) = 2sqrt(2).

working:
$$p=\sqrt{2mqV},\qquad \dfrac{\lambda_p}{\lambda_\alpha}=\sqrt{\dfrac{m_\alpha q_\alpha}{m_pq_p}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{(4m_p)(2e)}{m_pe}}=2\sqrt{2}$$

Independent check: For acceleration from rest, p = sqrt(2mqV) and wavelength is inversely proportional to momentum. Thus lambda_p/lambda_alpha = sqrt((4m_p)(2e)/(m_p e)) = 2sqrt(2).
solution:
For a particle accelerated from rest through potential $V$, $p=\sqrt{2mqV}$ and $\lambda=h/p$. Thus,
$$\frac{\lambda_p}{\lambda_\alpha}=\sqrt{\frac{m_\alpha q_\alpha}{m_pq_p}}=\sqrt{\frac{(4m_p)(2e)}{m_pe}}=2\sqrt{2}$$
Hence, $\lambda_p:\lambda_\alpha=2\sqrt{2}:1$.
